themes_detail.label: Street Signs Deteriorating Rapidly
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints spiked to 13 THIS WEEK, a 300% increase from the 3.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.59), suggesting sudden infrastructure degradation across Far Rockaway that may reflect deferred maintenance or weather damage.
evidence: 13 street sign damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.2 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 6.59)
Emerged suddenly this week with no prior escalation in recent weeks
Statistically significant deviation suggests systemic rather than isolated problem
reporting_angles: Canvas affected blocks to document what happened—weather event, poor maintenance, or vandalism?
Interview DOT about repair timeline and whether Rockaway receives proportional street maintenance funding
Cross-reference with pothole/street condition complaints (1,012 total over 90 days) to determine if sign damage is part of broader infrastructure crisis

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Crisis Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints surged to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO (3100% spike from 0.1 weekly baseline), a z-score of 11.72 (highest severity in dataset), signaling potential contamination or system failure that may pose public health risk.
evidence: 4 water quality complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% spike, z-score 11.72—highest in dataset)
Related: 337 water system complaints and 331 plumbing complaints over 90 days, suggesting chronic system stress
DEP has standing budget request for capital projects on sanitary sewer infrastructure, indicating known deficiency
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint details from 2 weeks ago—what specific water quality issues were reported (discoloration, odor, taste)?
Contact DEP for water testing results and any advisories for Far Rockaway; cross-check with health department
Interview affected residents and plumbers about frequency of water issues; investigate whether aging Rockaway infrastructure is failing

themes_detail.label: Dead Trees & Environmental Degradation
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints jumped to 6 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1100% increase from 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 11.0), indicating rapid environmental decline that may reflect storm damage, disease, or deferred park maintenance.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score 11.0)
Parks budget repeatedly requests funding for park reconstruction/upgrades, suggesting deferred maintenance
May indicate post-storm damage or tree disease outbreak requiring immediate intervention
reporting_angles: Visit affected locations and photograph dead trees; determine if concentrated in specific parks or scattered
Interview Parks Department about tree health assessments and removal/replanting timeline in Rockaway
Investigate whether storm from recent weeks (check weather data) caused mass tree damage; assess equity—is Rockaway getting resources for restoration?

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicle Backlog Worsening
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints reached 21 LAST WEEK, doubling the 10.1 weekly average (107% spike, z-score: 3.09), while abandoned vehicles remain a top 311 complaint category (289 over 90 days), suggesting NYPD/Sanitation is not keeping pace with removals.
evidence: 21 derelict vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 10.1 weekly average (107% spike, z-score 3.09)
289 abandoned vehicle complaints over 90 days (top-10 category), indicating chronic problem
Illegal parking also extremely high at 1,198 complaints over 90 days, suggesting street space under pressure
reporting_angles: Document specific streets with highest derelict vehicle concentration; calculate time-to-removal from 311 report date
Interview NYPD/Sanitation about resource constraints and whether Rockaway gets lower priority for vehicle removals
Talk to residents about quality-of-life impact—do derelict cars breed crime, rats, or blight?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping & Sanitation Decline
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints spiked to 15 THREE WEEKS AGO (145% above baseline of 6.1 weekly, z-score: 4.03), while unsanitary conditions remain endemic (366 complaints over 90 days), suggesting environmental enforcement gaps in a waterfront community already dealing with the Rockaway Whale incident.
evidence: 15 illegal dumping complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 6.1 weekly baseline (145% spike, z-score 4.03)
366 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days (top-10 category)
City Limits published environmental opinion piece on Rockaway Whale (May 5, 2026), indicating ecosystem/sanitation concerns are newsworthy in this community
reporting_angles: Map illegal dumping hotspots and interview residents about whether dumping correlates with specific vacant lots or waterfront access points
Interview DSNY/NYPD about enforcement capacity—why isn't dumping being prevented or prosecuted?
Connect to broader Rockaway waterfront health narrative: Is the community being treated as a dumping ground while major development projects (Edgemere, Arverne, 14-10 Beach Channel) proceed?
